- **E-JOINT and E-TIES SURVIVE** the twelve pin files (370 / 370), as the author states — the line's "pinning the
  order, the ties and the joint ends" is not met. CONFIRMED.
- **E-WIDE**: no fixture. My E-WIDE (pass 5's landing list and `verticesWithin` at 2 · FIDELITY_SQ) SURVIVES (370 / 370).
  The author's reason — "noSeat is false wherever class E fires: §3.10 keeps every vertex and non-incident edge ≥ minEdge
  off the piece, so every lattice point of its ≥ 137 cm chord keeps (ii) / (iii)" — does not hold: a split seat is a
  lattice point up to the hot pixel (0.71 cm) OFF the piece, and §3.10 only keeps other geometry ≥ minEdge from the piece
  itself. Construction (`s15/probe/ewide.py`, noseat.ts's tests transcribed): the level-0 piece (0, 0)–(2000, 10) (no
  lattice point strictly inside it between x = 0 and x = 200), finer (level 1) parallel edges (−k, 25k)–(2000 − k,
  25k + 10), k = ±1 … ±6, each 5001 / √40001 = 25.0047 cm from the next (§3.10 clearance: 0 violations); the chain
  point c = (100, 20), 19.5 cm off the piece: within the bound **no seat, no free spot, no vertex — noSeat TRUE**; within
  √2 · bound one seat, the on-line lattice point (200, 1) (101.8 cm from c), and the piece's end (0, 0). So the class
  admits exactly the fixture the line asks for (a seat in (bound, √2 · bound]); whether the router refuses it class E
  is the fixture's to show. CONFIRMED (the arithmetic); the router's outcome on it not run.
- The residual: noSeat certifies nothing (false on all 14 router-set refusals), so class E's census residual stays
  carried '(notBuilt #2, M4)' with no J238 (1) proof — C-0490 (2), (4). A bare carry under RL1. CONFIRMED (C-0490 read).
